business_problem: Caseworkers in Landratsamt Augsburg's Youth Welfare Office had to manually research legal references, citizen-submitted documents, and other records before working a case, making the process slow, labor intensive, and prone to errors during a staffing shortage.
solution_summary: Landratsamt Augsburg teamed with IBM Client Engineering and IBM Consulting to prototype a generative-AI case-research assistant for youth welfare staff. After workshops and a three-day hackathon, the joint team built a customized web application integrated with IBM watsonx Assistant, IBM watsonx.ai, and IBM Watson Discovery. The application queries multiple disparate sources defined by the client, retrieves supporting material, and summarizes findings for each welfare case so staff can compile the legal and financial context faster. Watson Discovery provides retrieval across the various references and submitted documents, watsonx.ai performs summarization, and watsonx Assistant supplies the conversational interface for the web app. The pilot showed that a workflow that could take up to an hour to compile manually could be reduced to a few minutes, giving the office a safer path to using gen AI in a sensitive public-sector process.

business_outcome: The pilot materially reduced case-compilation time, improved the quality of generated summaries, and showed Landratsamt Augsburg how gen AI could free caseworkers to focus more on citizens and less on repetitive research work.
